Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) First Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan I) (c. 600 AD)

OPENS Ch 16: post-Hellenistic-Roman GEOGRAPHIC CATALOG listing heathen peoples whose lands and rulers serve as God's instruments. The toponym-list is DIAGNOSTICALLY POST-HELLENISTIC: **Arabia + Parthia + Seleucia + Cappadocia + Pontus + Caesarea** all belong to the Hellenistic-Roman geographic horizon. **Parthia** (Eastern Empire 247 BC - 224 AD) + **Seleucia** (Hellenistic Syria-and-Mesopotamia 312-63 BC) + **Cappadocia** (Persian/Hellenistic Anatolia, Roman province from 17 AD) + **Pontus** (Hellenistic kingdom of Mithridates, Roman province from 64 BC) + **Caesarea** (Herodian foundation c. 22-10 BC, named for Augustus) form a TERMINUS-A-QUO of c. 1st c. CE. This dating-anchor pairs with 1 Mq 36:29 (Apollon + Artemis + Serapion cult-dating pre-400 CE) to bracket the chapter's composition to roughly 1st-4th c. CE — overlapping the early Aksumite period. Per Horovitz 1905 + CROSS_REFERENCE_APPENDIX §61: this is one of the strongest internal-dating clusters in 1 Mq.
